purpose: Define how MathBridge compares grade/year placement without inventing one-to-one equivalence between China, England and US systems.

concept_aligned.rule: Start from the selected Chinese concept and show the verified curriculum stage/year/grade where the same concept appears in the comparison system. Different grade numbers are allowed and should remain visible.

selected_grade_context.label_cn: 查看同年级标签的课程内容
selected_grade_context.label_en: View the same numbered grade/year label
selected_grade_context.rule: Show the requested grade/year content as context only. Do not call it equivalent unless concept evidence independently supports the alignment.

age_context.rule: Age information may be displayed later as contextual metadata. It must not be used as the curriculum mapping key and must not override verified concept placement.

china_resolution.national_standard: Use the 2022 national learning stage when exact current textbook placement is not verified.
china_resolution.current_pep: Use exact Grade N / semester / unit only when current-edition PEP evidence directly verifies it.
china_resolution.fallback: Never fill a missing current PEP grade from a legacy textbook sequence.

england_resolution.rule: Use statutory National Curriculum in England Year 1-6 placement.
england_resolution.display: Use England Year N; do not translate Year N into 中国N年级.

us_resolution.baseline: Use Common Core Grade N only when no state is selected.
us_resolution.states: When California or Texas is selected and a mapped state standard exists, use that state grade placement as the curriculum layer.
us_resolution.missing_state_mapping: Say the state-specific mapping is not yet available; do not silently substitute Common Core as the state requirement.

alignment_output.rule: alignment_type describes placement relationship only; it is not a judgement that two curricula have identical depth, pedagogy or assessment.

rendering_rules: Never hide different year/grade numbers to make the comparison look cleaner.
Do not use age as a proxy for curriculum equivalence.
Where China is stage-level and England/US is year-specific, show that difference explicitly.
If the same concept appears over several years, show a progression range rather than selecting one arbitrary equivalent year.
Depth, representations, procedures and reasoning expectations are compared separately from placement.
